ECDSA.note: NIST P-256 point-addition circuit; applies to any 256-bit prime-field curve

RSA-2048.source: Gidney & Ekerå, Quantum 5, 433 (2021) (arXiv:1905.09749); Gidney (arXiv:2505.15917) later reduces the physical-qubit requirement to under one million
RSA-2048.note: the anchor primitive: the expert survey asks specifically about RSA-2048

symmetric.source: NIST PQC security categories (AES-128/192/256 define levels 1/3/5); Jaques, Naehrig, Roetteler & Virdia, EUROCRYPT 2020 (arXiv:1910.01700)

conservative.name: conservative
conservative.source: Mosca & Piani, Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025, Global Risk Institute / evolutionQ (26 experts): CRQC within 10 years 28-49%, within 15 years 51-70%. Earlier editions place a break within 5 years at under 1%. Low end of each published range.

central.name: central
central.source: Mosca & Piani, Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025, Global Risk Institute / evolutionQ (26 experts): CRQC within 10 years 28-49%, within 15 years 51-70%. Earlier editions place a break within 5 years at under 1%. Midpoint of each published range.

aggressive.name: aggressive
aggressive.source: Mosca & Piani, Quantum Threat Timeline Report 2025, Global Risk Institute / evolutionQ (26 experts): CRQC within 10 years 28-49%, within 15 years 51-70%. Earlier editions place a break within 5 years at under 1%. High end of each published range.

tier_b_stated_assumption.why: converts a published resource ratio into a time offset; not calibrated, swept in qshield.experiments.calibration_sensitivity

tier_c_unobservable.why: no literature supplies these for a specific estate; handled by qshield.experiments.robustness, not by calibration

pqc_residual_risk.source: not a quantum-susceptibility estimate: a placeholder for cryptanalytic and implementation risk in a young primitive, carried over from earlier versions

not_calibrated_against_outcomes: No CRQC exists and nothing has been compromised via Shor's algorithm, so there are no outcome events to fit against. These are published estimates substituted for invented constants, which is not the same as a model validated against reality.
